description: Cut the sorted list at the 10th row's value and keep every row tied with it.

b.request: For each district, calculate account count and share, then return all districts that rank in the top 10 by difference (share minus average share), including all districts with a value equal to the 10th-highest difference, sorted descending.
b.sql:
WITH all_districts AS (
  SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS FLOAT) as num_districts
  FROM district
),
district_accounts AS (
  SELECT 
    d.district_id,
    COALESCE(COUNT(a.account_id), 0) as account_count
  FROM district d
  LEFT JOIN account a ON d.district_id = a.district_id
  GROUP BY d.district_id
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(account_count) as total_accounts
  FROM district_accounts
),
district_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    da.district_id,
    da.account_count,
    CAST(da.account_count AS FLOAT) / t.total_accounts as share,
    CAST(da.account_count AS FLOAT) / t.total_accounts - (1.0 / ad.num_districts) as difference
  FROM district_accounts da
  CROSS JOIN totals t
  CROSS JOIN all_districts ad
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    *,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY difference DESC) as rnk
  FROM district_stats
),
threshold AS (
  SELECT difference
  FROM ranked
  WHERE rnk = 10
)
SELECT 
  d.district_id,
  d.A2 as district_name,
  r.account_count,
  r.share,
  r.difference
FROM ranked r
JOIN district d ON r.district_id = d.district_id
WHERE r.difference >= (SELECT difference FROM threshold)
ORDER BY r.difference DESC
b.raw: For each district, calculate account count and share, then return all districts that rank in the top 10 by difference (share minus average share), including all districts with a value equal to the 10th-highest difference, sorted descending.

a.request: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), count its accounts and work out its share of all accounts (its count divided by the total number of accounts). Show the district id, the account count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share across districts (share minus that average). Sort by that difference from highest to lowest and return the top 10, plus any other districts tied with the 10th. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH total_accounts AS (SELECT COUNT(*)::REAL as total FROM account), district_accounts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) as account_count FROM account GROUP BY district_id), num_districts AS (SELECT COUNT(*) as num FROM district_accounts), with_difference AS (SELECT da.district_id, da.account_count, da.account_count::REAL / ta.total as share, da.account_count::REAL / ta.total - 1.0 / nd.num as difference FROM district_accounts da CROSS JOIN total_accounts ta CROSS JOIN num_districts nd) SELECT district_id, account_count, share, difference FROM with_difference WHERE difference >= (SELECT MIN(difference) FROM (SELECT difference FROM with_difference ORDER BY difference DESC LIMIT 10) as top_10) ORDER BY difference DESC

d.request: For each branch district, count accounts, calculate share and difference from average share, order by difference descending, and return all districts whose difference value is at least as large as the 10th-ranked difference value.
d.sql:
WITH account_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    district_id,
    COUNT(*) as account_count
  FROM account
  GROUP BY district_id
),
totals AS (
  SELECT 
    COUNT(*) as total_accounts,
    COUNT(DISTINCT district_id) as num_districts
  FROM account
),
with_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    ac.district_id,
    ac.account_count,
    CAST(ac.account_count AS FLOAT) / t.total_accounts as share,
    CAST(ac.account_count AS FLOAT) / t.total_accounts - 1.0 / t.num_districts as difference
  FROM account_counts ac
  CROSS JOIN totals t
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    district_id,
    account_count,
    share,
    difference,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY difference DESC) as rn
  FROM with_shares
),
tenth_threshold AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(
    (SELECT difference FROM ranked WHERE rn = 10),
    (SELECT MIN(difference) FROM ranked)
  ) as threshold
)
SELECT 
  district_id,
  account_count,
  share,
  difference
FROM ranked
WHERE difference >= (SELECT threshold FROM tenth_threshold)
ORDER BY difference DESC

c.request: For each branch district (`account.district_id`), count its accounts and work out its share of all accounts (its count divided by the total number of accounts). Show the district id, the account count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share across districts (share minus that average). Which are the top 10 districts by that difference, from highest to lowest? Don't round anything. Cut the sorted list at the 10th row's value and keep every row tied with it.
c.sql:
WITH district_accounts AS (
  SELECT 
    account.district_id,
    COUNT(*) as account_count
  FROM account
  GROUP BY account.district_id
),
total_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total FROM account
),
with_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    da.district_id,
    da.account_count,
    da.account_count / CAST(tc.total AS FLOAT) as share
  FROM district_accounts da
  CROSS JOIN total_count tc
),
with_avg_diff AS (
  SELECT 
    district_id,
    account_count,
    share,
    share - AVG(share) OVER () as difference
  FROM with_shares
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    district_id,
    account_count,
    share,
    difference,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY difference DESC) as row_num
  FROM with_avg_diff
),
threshold AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT difference FROM ranked WHERE row_num = 10),
      (SELECT MIN(difference) FROM ranked)
    ) as cutoff
)
SELECT 
  district_id,
  account_count,
  share,
  difference
FROM ranked
WHERE difference >= (SELECT cutoff FROM threshold)
ORDER BY difference DESC, district_id
